result.rationale: The handler builds EventManager from the calling user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, while authorization explicitly permits non-organizer callers (`isTeamAdminOrOwner`, `isAttendee`). So when an attendee or team admin calls addGuests, calendar attendee updates run against the caller's calendar credentials/destinationCalendar rather than the booking organizer's (`evt.destinationCalendar` comes from the booking organizer, but credentials are the caller's), which can fail or update the wrong calendar account. adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, line 161-165 shows `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and then `new EventManager({...user, credentials: [...credentials]})`. The ctx.user is the current caller (who could be an attendee or team admin per the permission check on lines 47-53), not the booking organizer. The booking organizer's credentials are fetched in the booking query (line 38-39 includes user.credentials) but never used. This means calendar updates will use the wrong credentials when an attendee or team admin adds guests.
